sentences.text: Alleging that the respondent police has not properly investigated the matter, the present petition in Crl.O.P.No.15865 of 2023 has been filed to transfer the investigation to some other agency, such as CBCID.

2. The complaint as such indicates that on the promise that a valuable property sold in auction by the Debt Recovery Tribunal under SARFAESI Act will be retrieved, a sum of Rs.15,00,00,000/- has been transferred by the complainant to the account of Lingam & Co., which was owned and managed by the first accused.
The petitioner breached the promise, which he made with an intention to cheat.
The police is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis investigating the case for the offences under Sections 120-B, 420, 406, 463, 464, 471, 506(2) IPC.
3. In this case, R.S.Ganesan, is a third party.
Whereas the second accused Vidhya Balachandar is the relative of the defacto complainant.
The defacto complainant alleges that the police not showing interest to investigate the matter properly, which has led to screening of the evidence and diversion of the money cheated.
4. The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side), on instruction, states that the investigation has been done effectively and so far six witnesses have been examined.
The first accused was secured and remanded before the Judicial Magistrate.
However, the Judicial Magistrate disinclined to remand him to judicial custody and thereafter, he has been called for enquiry.
On completion of i n v e s t i g a t i o n , f i n a l r e p o r t w i l l b e f i l e d p r o b a b l y w i t h i n t h r e e m o n t h s .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
In the light of the undertaking given by the learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side), this Original Petition filed to transfer the investigation stands dismissed.

6. As far as the second accused is concerned, who is the petitioner in Crl.O.P.No.31586 of 2022, the learned Government Advocate(Crl.Side) further submitted that she has been already granted Anticipatory bail on condition that she should deposit a sum of Rs.3,00,00,000/- but she did not deposit the same and therefore, as per the order of this Court, the anticipatory bail granted automatically stands dismissed.
He further states that necessary efforts have been taken to secure the second accused and proceed in accordance with law.
7. Since the petitioner had not complied the condition, no fresh bail petition need be entertained.
Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition is dismissed.

8. In Crl.O.P.No.10864 of 2023, R.S.Ganesan, the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis herein apprehending arrest by the respondent police has moved this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail.
9. It appears, that pending anticipatory bail, the petitioner was secured and produced before the learned Judicial Magistrate.
However, the Judicial Magistrate had refused to remand him.
As a consequence, the petitioner has been let out on bail in the Station itself.
Therefore, nothing survives in this petition.
Hence, this Criminal Original Petition is dismissed.
